image.subject: 臺北松山機場／Taipei Songshan Airport (TSA)
image.description: 2026年4月19日由觀景地點拍攝的臺北松山機場資料照片；並非2026年10月23日颱風影響現場。

zh.title: 薔琵颱風衝擊松山機場　10月23日國內線全取消、多班國際線異動
zh.summary: 強烈颱風薔琵逼近，臺北松山機場公布10月23日航班異動：國內線全數取消，日本航空、華航、中國東方航空等多家業者的國際與兩岸航班停飛；全日空NH853、NH854提前，日航JL99暫定順延至24日。實際班表以航空公司最新通知為準。
body: 受強烈颱風薔琵（Champi）影響，臺北松山機場（TSA）公布10月23日（星期五）航班異動，國內航線全數取消，國際及兩岸航線則有多家航空公司宣布停飛或調整時刻。松山機場表示，原公告將視情況持續更新，旅客須以各航空公司最新發布的航班動態與通知為準。以下整理截至10月22日晚間由機場公布、使用者提供的航班異動內容，屬預定調整，並非10月23日實際執飛結果。
國內線方面，松山機場宣布10月23日所有國內線航班取消。交通部民用航空局同日亦指出，根據國籍航空公司提供的最新資訊，10月23日全臺國內航線將全日停飛。旅客如原訂往返澎湖、金門、馬祖或其他國內目的地，應先確認航班取消通知及各航空公司的改票、退票規定。
日本航線方面，日本航空（Japan Airlines／JAL）取消10月23日JL96、JL97與JL98航班；JL99原訂當日航班則規劃延至10月24日11時，是否如期執行仍依日航後續公告。全日本空輸（ANA）則將NH853調整至13時50分、NH854調整至14時50分，兩班均較原定時刻提前；上述時間均依松山機場公告列示，跨境航班起降時區與實際時刻須以航空公司確認為準。
中華航空（China Airlines）取消10月23日CI223、CI221及CI222航班，涉及松山與東京羽田機場（HND）間航線。機場公告將取消班號列為CI223及CI221／CI222，並未宣告華航所有松山航班均取消，未列入名單的航班仍須另行查詢。

兩岸航線方面，中國東方航空（China Eastern Airlines）的MU5097、MU5098取消；上海航空（Shanghai Airlines）的FM851、FM852、FM801及FM802取消；廈門航空（XiamenAir）的MF881、MF882取消，四川航空（Sichuan Airlines）的3U3981、3U3982、3U3783及3U3784亦列入取消名單。中國國際航空（Air China）的CA197、CA198同樣取消。
往返韓國的航班也受影響，德威航空（T'way Air）10月23日TW667與TW668取消。前述航班為松山機場當次公告明確列出的取消名單，並不代表未列出班號的所有國際航班均照常飛航。
民航局指出，受颱風影響，航空公司可能持續調整國際航班，並已要求航空公司在官方網站公布資訊、主動通知旅客。民航局也協調航空公司事先規劃颱風後的疏運運能，必要時啟動備援安排；航班恢復時程仍須依天候、機組與航機調度及各航空公司通知確認。
松山機場提醒搭機旅客及接機民眾，出發前應先查看航空公司官方網站、手機應用程式或通知簡訊，並以航空公司公告的最新起降時刻及取消狀態為準；航班資訊亦可參閱松山機場官網及其官方Facebook粉絲專頁。此篇為10月22日已公布資訊之整理，後續若有變更，應以官方即時消息為準。

en.title: Typhoon Champi Disrupts Taipei Songshan Airport (TSA): All Domestic Flights Canceled for October 23
en.summary: Taipei Songshan Airport says all domestic flights on October 23 will be canceled as Typhoon Champi approaches Taiwan. Multiple international and cross-strait flights operated by JAL, China Airlines and other carriers are also canceled, while ANA has brought forward two services and JAL plans to defer JL99 until October 24. Airline advisories remain the definitive source for changes.
body: Taipei Songshan Airport (TSA) has announced extensive flight disruptions for Friday, October 23, 2026, as strong Typhoon Champi approaches Taiwan. All domestic flights are set to be canceled, while multiple international and cross-strait services have been canceled or rescheduled. The airport said its notices may be updated as conditions change. The details below reflect the airport's October 22 advisory supplied for this report, rather than confirmed flight outcomes on October 23.

For domestic operations, Songshan Airport said every flight scheduled for October 23 would be canceled. Taiwan's Civil Aviation Administration separately confirmed that all domestic air services across the country would be suspended for the day, based on the latest information provided by Taiwanese airlines. Travelers bound for Penghu, Kinmen, Matsu or other domestic destinations should check cancellation notices and each carrier's rebooking and refund policy.

On services to Japan, Japan Airlines (JAL) has canceled flights JL96, JL97 and JL98 scheduled for October 23. Flight JL99 is tentatively postponed to 11:00 on October 24, subject to further confirmation by JAL. All Nippon Airways (ANA) has brought forward NH853 to 13:50 and NH854 to 14:50 according to the Songshan Airport notice. Travelers should verify the relevant local departure and arrival times directly with the airlines.

China Airlines has canceled flights CI223, CI221 and CI222 on October 23, affecting services between Songshan and Tokyo Haneda Airport (HND). The airport's list identifies these particular services; it does not amount to an announcement that every China Airlines flight operating at Songshan has been canceled.

Cross-strait disruptions include the cancellation of China Eastern Airlines flights MU5097 and MU5098; Shanghai Airlines flights FM851, FM852, FM801 and FM802; XiamenAir flights MF881 and MF882; and Sichuan Airlines flights 3U3981, 3U3982, 3U3783 and 3U3784. Air China flights CA197 and CA198 are also canceled.

Services to and from South Korea are affected as well, with T'way Air canceling flights TW667 and TW668 on October 23. The flights named in this report are those expressly listed in the airport advisory. A flight absent from the list should not be assumed to be operating normally without separate confirmation.

Taiwan's Civil Aviation Administration warned that international airline schedules could continue to change because of the typhoon. It has instructed carriers to publish updates on their official websites and notify passengers. Authorities have also been coordinating contingency capacity for passenger movement once conditions permit, although the timing of the recovery will depend on weather and operational arrangements.

Passengers and those meeting arriving travelers should check their airline's official website, app or direct notifications before heading to the airport. Further information is available from Songshan Airport's website and official Facebook page. This report summarizes the October 22 notice; all flight statuses and times remain subject to subsequent airline announcements.
